Send Task

General Concept: A Send Task in BPMN is used to send a message to an external participant or system. It is typically used for outbound communication, such as sending notifications, events, or data to another process or service.

 

TaktX Implementation: In TaktX, a Send Task is executed by the engine using a configured message handler. You can define input mappings using FEEL expressions to prepare the message payload. Send Tasks support error handling and timeouts. Variable scoping ensures only mapped variables are sent. The engine can interact with messaging systems, APIs, or custom adapters for outbound communication.

Usage & Options in TaktX:
A Send Task in TaktX allows you to:

  • Define input mappings using FEEL expressions to prepare the message payload.
  • Configure error handling and timeouts for reliable delivery.
  • Limit variable scope to only mapped variables for security and clarity.
  • Integrate with messaging systems, APIs, or custom adapters for outbound communication.
  • Monitor execution and audit results via the TaktX client.
  • Attach boundary events for error, escalation, or timer handling.

 

Example: Order Process with Send Task

 

This example shows a process where an order is placed, a Send Task notifies the shipping system, and the process continues to shipment confirmation. The Send Task demonstrates outbound integration with external systems.

Tips & Tricks:

  • Use FEEL expressions to format and validate message payloads.
  • Configure error handling for reliable delivery.
  • Limit the scope of variables to only those needed in the message.
  • Document message formats and endpoints.

Pitfalls:

  • Unmapped variables will not be included in the message.
  • Handle delivery errors and timeouts to avoid process interruptions.
  • Ensure message endpoints are reachable and properly secured.
